decisions.title: Supported server and client versions
decisions.section: REST API specification and server semantics
decisions.issue: OpenSearch server patches, major versions, plugins, distributions, and official client releases can expose different accepted requests and observable results.
interpretations: Claim broad 2.x and 3.x compatibility from the client API.
Publish only the exact server and client combinations exercised by the release matrix.
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenSearch 2.19.6 and 3.8.0 agree on the adapter's maintained shared-semantics differential; the official Go client 4.7.3 supplies the transport and signer boundary.
decisions.selected_behavior: The supported matrix is exactly OpenSearch 2.19.6, OpenSearch 3.8.0, and opensearch-go/v4 4.7.3; no other patch, plugin, analyzer, mapping, distribution, or managed-service profile is implied compatible.
decisions.rationale: Exact pins keep a reproducible compatibility claim and prevent a client version from standing in for server evidence.
decisions.security_consequences: Each newly supported server or client requires source, vulnerability, credential, and transport review.
decisions.resource_consequences: Both server versions run through the same bounded real-cluster matrix and release budgets.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Unlisted combinations remain unsupported until separately reviewed and exercised.
decisions.wire_consequences: Requests and accepted response shapes are guaranteed only for the exact matrix.
decisions.upstream_status: The OpenSearch project publishes separate server and client releases and does not provide this adapter's cross-version compatibility claim.
decisions.reconsider_when: A server, client, plugin, distribution, request shape, or response shape changes.

decisions.title: Endpoint, TLS, proxy, and credential trust
decisions.section: Client configuration, transport, retry, discovery, and signing
decisions.issue: The official client permits caller transports, retries, proxies, discovery, and credentials but does not define the adapter's authority, ownership, disclosure, or retry boundaries.
interpretations: Inherit client and environment defaults.
Require explicit bounded authorities, single-attempt backend requests, per-request credentials, and caller-visible transport ownership.
decisions.peer_behavior: The official client supports both permissive defaults and explicit configuration; this adapter deliberately selects the narrower explicit profile.
decisions.selected_behavior: Endpoints, TLS, proxies, discovery trust, transport ownership, admission, and credentials are explicit and bounded; credentials refresh per request, borrowed transport trust and proxy policy remain caller-owned, and every backend request is dispatched at most once even when one operation requires multiple bounded requests.
decisions.rationale: The application must own credential authority and ambiguous retry reconciliation instead of delegating either implicitly to transport defaults.
decisions.security_consequences: Unsafe schemes, URL userinfo, implicit adapter-configured proxies, untrusted discovered nodes, insecure credential transport, and secret-bearing diagnostics fail closed; caller-supplied borrowed transport trust remains caller-owned.
decisions.resource_consequences: Concurrency, queueing, response bodies, discovery results, and shutdown are bounded and all owned resources close on every path.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications relying on implicit environment proxying, client retries, or caller transport closure must configure those concerns explicitly outside the adapter.
decisions.wire_consequences: Each backend request is dispatched at most once by the adapter; ambiguous receipt is preserved rather than replayed.
decisions.upstream_status: This is an adapter trust and ownership profile over capabilities intentionally exposed by the official client.
decisions.reconsider_when: The official client changes transport ownership, retry, proxy, discovery, signer, or credential behavior.

decisions.title: Typed query surface and raw extensions
decisions.section: Search, point-in-time, search_after, Query DSL, and response APIs
decisions.issue: OpenSearch permits many query encodings, partial responses, raw DSL forms, and pagination mechanisms without defining tenant authorization, application cursor integrity, traversal budgets, or PIT cleanup ownership.
interpretations: Expose raw DSL and provider cursor identifiers.
Translate the portable typed contract and bind bounded signed cursors to the complete authorized search intent.
decisions.peer_behavior: OpenSearch 2.19.6 and 3.8.0 accept the deterministic generated DSL and return equivalent shared semantics in the maintained version differential.
decisions.selected_behavior: Search authorization precedes resolution; typed queries use deterministic package-owned JSON; raw extensions are explicit, bounded, and opensearch-bound; offset traversal is shallow, while PIT cursors bind tenant, query, projection, index fingerprint, totals, expiry, and cleanup ownership.
decisions.rationale: Deterministic encoding and application-owned cursors preserve portable intent, authorization scope, and finite backend resource ownership.
decisions.security_consequences: Untrusted DSL, analyzer names, physical topology, cross-tenant hits, cursor tampering, partial results, and provider bodies cannot escape validation.
decisions.resource_consequences: Query, projection, response, hit, aggregation, traversal, PIT count, and absolute lifetime limits apply before allocation or continuation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Ranking, mappings, analyzers, plugins, and raw extensions remain deployment-specific; cursor handoff is only compatible where explicitly exercised.
decisions.wire_consequences: Typed input maps to deterministic JSON, successful responses require complete attribution, and every terminal owned PIT path closes once.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenSearch defines provider APIs; tenant policy, portable query ownership, signed cursors, and cleanup responsibility are application decisions.
decisions.reconsider_when: The shared query contract, OpenSearch Query DSL, PIT lifecycle, response schemas, or cursor compatibility requirements change.

decisions.title: External-version writes and deletes
decisions.section: Index, delete, bulk, external versioning, and error response APIs
decisions.issue: Write transport loss and positional bulk responses can leave receipt or per-item attribution unknown, while internal versioning and update semantics cannot preserve source-of-truth ordering.
interpretations: Retry whole requests and trust positional success.
Use external versions, validate every item identity and action, and preserve failed, conflicted, not-found, and unknown outcomes separately.
decisions.peer_behavior: Both supported OpenSearch versions exercise attributed external-version indexing and deletion; provider error details still differ and are not public contract.
decisions.selected_behavior: Writes require a durable application guard and external versions; update-existing is unsupported; bulk results are positionally and structurally attributed, safe outcomes are classified per item, and ambiguous transport or malformed acknowledgements remain unknown without retry.
decisions.rationale: Derived search state must not overtake the source of truth or convert an unobserved write result into a fabricated terminal outcome.
decisions.security_consequences: Authorization and immutable bounded snapshots precede index resolution and provider error bodies are not exposed.
decisions.resource_consequences: Operation counts, encoded NDJSON bytes, response bytes, concurrency, and per-item metadata are strictly bounded.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers must reconcile unknown outcomes by document identity and external version; update-existing requires a different backend contract.
decisions.wire_consequences: Index, upsert, and delete use external version semantics, and bulk response action, index, ID, status, result, and version must match the request.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenSearch documents version modes and bulk shapes but cannot determine application source-of-truth authority or whether a lost response followed receipt.
decisions.reconsider_when: OpenSearch adds a versioned idempotency protocol or the shared write contract changes ordering or update semantics.

decisions.title: Lifecycle, reindex, verification, and alias cutover
decisions.section: Index, template, reindex, tasks, count, alias, and snapshot APIs
decisions.issue: Provider lifecycle APIs do not define application migration identity, authorization, durable exclusion, semantic equivalence, alias fencing, rollback, cleanup eligibility, or snapshot ownership.
interpretations: Call provider lifecycle APIs directly and treat count equality as readiness.
Require encrypted resumable state, semantic verification, a durable application fence, and guarded destructive cleanup.
decisions.peer_behavior: The exact 2.19.6 and 3.8.0 matrix exercises rebuild, reindex, semantic verification, alias cutover, rollback seams, cleanup exclusion, and deployment-owned snapshot restore.
decisions.selected_behavior: Lifecycle operations are separately authorized; reindex cursors are encrypted, expiring, and migration-bound; semantic verification gates fenced alias cutover; creation, alias mutation, cutover, and cleanup share durable exclusion; snapshot configuration and restore remain deployment-owned evidence.
decisions.rationale: Provider acknowledgements and equal counts cannot prove semantic migration safety or application-wide exclusion from concurrent writers and retained readers.
decisions.security_consequences: Physical generations, cursor task IDs, fingerprints, guard failures, snapshot locations, and destructive operations remain authenticated, bounded, redacted, and explicitly authorized.
decisions.resource_consequences: Polling, cursor size and lifetime, verification records, callbacks, task responses, retained PITs, and cleanup checks have finite budgets.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Changing fingerprints, cursor envelopes, verification policy, fence semantics, aliases, retention, or snapshot deployment requires migration and compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Cutover is emitted only after current fingerprint and semantic evidence; ambiguous mutations remain unknown, and deletion occurs only while the durable eligibility guard is held.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenSearch owns backend lifecycle and snapshot APIs; the application owns source-of-truth equivalence, write fencing, retention, backup infrastructure, and deletion authority.
decisions.reconsider_when: Provider lifecycle semantics, migration state, fingerprinting, semantic verification, application fencing, retention, or snapshot deployment changes.

decisions.issue: HTTP success, provider diagnostics, release feeds, and common peer behavior do not by themselves establish readiness, safe disclosure, or compatibility with a new server or API revision.

decisions.selected_behavior: Readiness requires complete bounded health and capacity signals; failures and telemetry expose stable classifications without backend bodies or private causes; mutable release authorities are digest-monitored, and any source or observable decision change is release-blocking until reviewed, recorded, and exercised.
decisions.rationale: Operational safety and compatibility require evidence at the adapter boundary rather than inference from status codes, release recency, or untrusted provider text.
decisions.security_consequences: Queries, documents, credentials, cursors, physical topology, raw errors, and observer panics cannot enter public failures or telemetry.

decisions.compatibility_consequences: New source digests, errata, releases, response requirements, classifications, or supported versions require a new reviewed decision digest and changelog record.
decisions.wire_consequences: Missing or malformed required operational fields fail closed and no release feed silently changes request or response behavior.
decisions.upstream_status: Release and errata feeds are monitoring signals, not authority to change adapter behavior automatically.

decisions.title: Search authorization precedes index resolution

decisions.title: Reindex continuation cursor
decisions.section: Historical adapter policy consolidated without changing observable behavior
decisions.issue: Asynchronous reindex returns a backend task ID but does not bind it to an application tenant, source generation, target generation, expiry, or safe path grammar. Returning the raw ID permits cross-operation substitution and exposes provider topology.
interpretations: Return raw task IDs, store task state in the adapter, accept caller-provided paths, or issue an encrypted opaque continuation. Operational clients usually expose the backend task directly.
decisions.peer_behavior: Return raw task IDs, store task state in the adapter, accept caller-provided paths, or issue an encrypted opaque continuation. Operational clients usually expose the backend task directly.
decisions.selected_behavior: Security, resource, compatibility, and wire consequences are included in the selected behavior below. Reindex continuation is a separate bounded AES-256-GCM cursor binding task ID, tenant, physical source, physical target, and bounded expiry without disclosing those values to the token holder. Tampering, unsafe task syntax, cross-binding reuse, expiry, and over-limit tokens fail before polling. Every successful incomplete poll reseals the same task binding with a fresh bounded lease, and callers must replace their durable cursor checkpoint. It does not share search-cursor keys or semantics.

decisions.title: Semantic verification gates alias cutover
decisions.section: Historical adapter policy consolidated without changing observable behavior
decisions.issue: Equal document counts do not prove that source and target generations contain the same IDs, external versions, source bytes, mappings, or settings. A caller-stored fingerprint does not attest live target state and sampling cannot safely authorize cutover.
interpretations: Trust count equality, sample records, compare only mappings, or require a full bounded semantic verifier. Reindex helpers commonly stop at task completion or count comparison.
decisions.peer_behavior: Trust count equality, sample records, compare only mappings, or require a full bounded semantic verifier. Reindex helpers commonly stop at task completion or count comparison.
decisions.selected_behavior: Security, resource, compatibility, and wire consequences are included in the selected behavior below. VerifyIndex performs count preflight and then requires a LifecycleVerifier to compare the complete bounded ID, external version, and canonical source-digest set from a stable point-in-time view and independently attest the live target definition fingerprint. Drift, missing attestation, impossible counts, or verifier failure prevents a verified report. CutoverAlias requires an application-owned LifecycleCutoverGuard that synchronously quiesces writes and retains that fence across a fresh complete verification and atomic alias mutation. Raw SwapAlias remains an explicitly unverified low-level primitive for bootstrap or already externally fenced recovery.

decisions.title: Snapshot restore is deployment-owned evidence

decisions.title: Destructive cleanup shares durable mutation exclusion
decisions.section: Historical adapter policy consolidated without changing observable behavior
decisions.issue: Alias inventory, retained-reader, retention, backup, and generation-identity checks occur separately from physical index deletion. Another application instance can otherwise create or re-alias the candidate after the final check and before deletion.
interpretations: Treat the check as advisory, rely on a process lock, expose raw deletion, or require one durable coordinator shared by every lifecycle mutation. OpenSearch does not provide one transaction spanning application prerequisites, alias inspection, and index deletion.
decisions.peer_behavior: Treat the check as advisory, rely on a process lock, expose raw deletion, or require one durable coordinator shared by every lifecycle mutation. OpenSearch does not provide one transaction spanning application prerequisites, alias inspection, and index deletion.
decisions.selected_behavior: CreateIndex, AddAlias, SwapAlias, CutoverAlias, and CleanupIndex require an application-owned LifecycleMutationGuard. It receives the tenant, operation, and complete resource set, invokes the mutation synchronously exactly once, and must hold cross-instance exclusion until the callback returns. Cleanup nests its final LifecycleCleanupGuard checks and deletion inside the same exclusion. Missing, repeated, asynchronous, or contradictory callbacks fail with a stable typed error and do not expose coordinator details. Security consequences: lifecycle authorization and exact resource validation still run before the durable exclusion, and guard failures expose no tenant, resource, lock, or coordinator details. Compatibility consequences: every application instance that enables lifecycle mutation must configure the same durable guard contract; process-local guards and mixed guarded/unguarded deployments are unsupported. Wire consequences: REST request and response shapes remain unchanged, but alias inspection and deletion execute inside one serialized callback and no hidden retry or extra mutation is introduced.
